title: Bose Is Buying Skullcandy. It’s Not as Weird as It Sounds
description: Bose, a longtime audio giant, has announced its acquisition of Skullcandy, the lifestyle brand known for bass-heavy, budget-friendly headphones. This move aims to expand Bose's reach to new consumer groups, particularly those connected with board sports culture and more affordable audio products. The acquisition retains Skullcandy's base in Park City, Utah, preserving its cultural roots.

sections.heading: Bose Strengthens Its Audio Portfolio
paragraphs: In October 2026, Bose announced the purchase of Skullcandy, a brand recognized for its energetic bass-heavy headphones and lifestyle appeal, especially among board sports enthusiasts. This acquisition complements Bose's premium audio offerings by adding a brand that connects with younger and more budget-conscious consumers.

Skullcandy will continue operating as a separate entity within Bose's Premium Consumer Audio division and will remain headquartered in Park City, Utah. Bose's CEO Lila Snyder emphasizes the value of Skullcandy's strong community connections and cultural relevance, qualities that Bose seeks to incorporate.

sections.heading: Strategic Partnership Preceded the Acquisition
paragraphs: Before the acquisition, Bose had already been involved with Skullcandy through its Sound by Bose licensing program, providing audio expertise for Skullcandy's products starting with the Method 360 ANC earbuds in 2025 and continuing with the Crusher 1080 ANC headphones in 2026.

Skullcandy's CEO Brian Garofalow remarked that while the company excels in building culture and community, it has acknowledged challenges in engineering innovation. Bose’s audio expertise fills this gap, making the partnership—and now acquisition—a natural progression.

sections.heading: Significance and Future Outlook
paragraphs: This acquisition allows Bose to offer products at both the premium and budget ends of the audio market, contrasting with its previous acquisitions such as the McIntosh Group, which focuses on luxury audio.

Keeping Skullcandy in Utah supports the brand’s authentic connection to board sports culture, ensuring it remains rooted where it originated. The deal positions Bose to expand into consumer segments it had previously struggled to reach, marking a notable shift in its business strategy.
